That winter, Lu'ay's mother was ill, so Lu'ay carried water from the well every morning, and his two jars were heavy for him.

His friend Marwan said to him, "I'll help you. I'll wait for you at the well tomorrow at dawn."

When morning came, Marwan got out of bed and found it bitterly cold, while his bed was so warm.

He said to himself, "If I slept a little longer… Lu'ay wouldn't be upset." Then he remembered that he had promised, and he got up.

He found Lu'ay at the well waiting for him, his hands red with cold.

They pulled up the bucket together, filled both jars, and each of them carried one.

It became an everyday thing. Marwan would say, "We meet at the well at dawn," and he was never late.

Then came a Sunday with no school.

On Saturday evening, two boys from the neighbourhood came to Marwan with a paper kite and said, "Tomorrow at dawn we're going out to the valley — the wind is strong there. Come with us!"

Marwan was thrilled and said, "Yes!"

When he went inside, he remembered Lu'ay and the well. He sat there torn: the valley and the kite on one side, and the two jars on the other.

He said, "Lu'ay can carry the water by himself for one day."

But he remembered that Lu'ay did not know about the trip, and that he would stand at the well in the cold, waiting for him.

And he remembered an ayah their teacher had recited: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ ۖ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا﴾

So he went out to the two boys and said, "I have a meeting at dawn that I can't miss. You go, and I'll catch up with you afterwards."

They said, "What meeting is that?" So he told them.

At dawn Marwan went to the well — and the two boys came with him, saying, "We'll fill the jars together, and then we'll all go to the valley."

The four of them filled the two jars in minutes.

Then they carried the water to Lu'ay's house, and they all went out to the valley and flew the kite until noon.

And Lu'ay would say, "I've never seen a friend who keeps his word like Marwan."

﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ ۖ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا﴾

📖 Al-Isra' 34. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
